newsitem.title: HUNGARY: FOCUS - Egis stable after Q1 earnings.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Egis stable after Q1 earnings.

text.p: Shares in major Hungarian pharmaceuticals company Egis Gyogyszergyar Rt opened unchanged on the Budapest Stock Exchange on Wednesday, following the release of its January-March earnings report.
Egis defied analysts' expectation of a decline on the bourse and opened at 10,600 forints, unchanged from Tuesday's close. At 1035 GMT it traded at 10,650.
Traders said the stock was in modest demand on the bourse with investors ready to buy at around 10,200 forints, below the price at which sellers were prepared to unload.
"There would be sellers, but the buying side is weak," one trader said.
Egis is a leader on the Hungarian market in terms of market share of around 12 percent, and also has one of the largest capitalisations of 84.83 billion forints at end-March.

Majority-owned by France's Servier S.A., it reported after-tax profit of 1.796 billion forints for the first three months of 1997, up from 1.651 billion in the same period of 1996. Net sales rose to 6.899 billion foirnts from 6.125 billion.
The company said its domestic sales remained below target, while exports and profits were in line with budget in the first quarter.
Analysts said the profit picture was modest but they praised the improvement in exports to 3.401 billion forints from 2.089 billion in the first three months of 1996.
"The growth in exports is a major development because Egis had signalled that it would like to boost the proportion of its exports within sales," said Rudi Voros, analyst at ICE Securities in London.
In 1996 domestic sales accounted for 54.9 percent of Egis's total sales and the company expected this ratio to drop to 52 percent in 1997 and to below 50 percent in 1998.
The proportion of exports has been around two-thirds for one of the market's other pharmaceuticals companies, Richter Gedeon Rt.
"Very often when investors compare Egis and Richter, Richter is assessed better because a bigger part of its sales is generated on export markets," Voros said.
"Therefore Egis has been bought at lower multiples and I guess this will remain so."
In the first three months of 1997 Egis's domestic sales of 3.498 billion forints remained 13 percent below the domestic turnover of the same period of last year and it was also short of plans.

"In the first quarter of 1996 wholesalers purchased substantial stocks of medicines in anticipation of price increases, while this did not characterise the market in the beginning of 1997," the company said in its earnings report.
The company's costs grew more sharply than its total sales, with direct costs up 16.1 percent and indirect costs up 13.9 percent, compared to a 12.6 percent rise in total sales.
"Cost items grew at a faster rate than sales, the simple consequence is that operating profits grew only by a very small margin of 2.2 percent, which is obviously a disappointment," Voros said.
This 2.2 percent figure compares to Egis's plan to boost operating profit by 16 percent this year.
Nevertheless, the market generally maintains its positive opinion on Egis which has good opportunities to further benefit from its partnership with Servier.
"Egis is a good quality company, with a strong management," Voros said.

"The synergies to the partnership with the French partner eventually will show some positive effects, but previously, I believe, people saw the positive effects coming through much more quickly," ICE's analyst said.
